name: Salsa Verde Enchiladas
desc: Flour tortillas spread with mashed black beans, filled with poblano, tomato, and whole beans, baked under green salsa and Monterey Jack.

source.title: Salsa Verde Enchiladas with Poblano Pepper, Black Beans & Monterey Jack Cheese
source.evidence: Same meal-kit amounts (13.4 oz black beans, 1 tbsp Southwest Spice Blend, 6 flour tortillas, 7 oz green salsa, 1/4 cup Monterey Jack, 2 tbsp sour cream) and the same 475°F top-rack bake with a spiced sour cream crema.

ingredients.raw: 1 poblano pepper, cored, seeded, and diced
2 scallions, thinly sliced, whites and greens separated
ingredients.prep: thinly sliced, whites and greens separated

ingredients.raw: 1 (13.4 oz) carton black beans, drained with liquid reserved
ingredients.note: 13.4 oz carton; a 15 oz can works

ingredients.raw: 1 small fresh chili pepper (such as jalapeño or Fresno), thinly sliced
1 tbsp HelloFresh Southwest Spice Blend (or 1 tbsp taco seasoning), divided
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Adjust a rack to the top position and preheat the oven to 475°F. Prep the poblano, tomato, scallions, and chili. Drain the beans over a small bowl, keeping the liquid.
Set aside 1/2 tsp of the Southwest spice in a small bowl for the crema.
Heat a drizzle of the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the poblano until just softened, 3-4 min.

Add the tomato, scallion whites, half the beans, 2 tbsp reserved bean liquid, and the rest of the Southwest spice. Cook, stirring, until fragrant and warmed through, 2-3 min. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pot over medium-high heat. Add the rest of the beans and cook until slightly softened, 2-3 min. Add 3 tbsp reserved bean liquid and simmer 1-2 min.
Reduce the heat to low, stir in the butter, turn off the heat, and mash with a fork or potato masher until mostly smooth. Season well with salt and pepper.
Spread each tortilla with mashed beans, spoon some filling onto one half, and roll up from the filled side. Place seam side down in an 8x11 in baking dish.
Spoon enough salsa over to coat generously and sprinkle with the Monterey Jack. Bake on the top rack until the salsa bubbles and the cheese melts, 3-5 min.
Meanwhile, stir the sour cream into the reserved spice, adding warm water 1 tsp at a time until it drizzles. Season with salt and pepper.
Drizzle the enchiladas with the crema and top with the scallion greens and as much sliced chili as you like.
